text:
Alex Formenton is back in the NHL after years away, including a stint in Switzerland with Ambrì-Piotta, and he's playing a depth role in Edmonton, about 13 minutes a night. He has two goals and five points in 18 games, with 47 hits.

The on-ice numbers are rough. Edmonton has taken 37% of the expected goals with him on the ice, about 14 points worse than without him, and the Oilers have actually scored about six more goals than expected in his minutes, so the results are flattering the process. His ice time has dropped by nearly three minutes a night over his last ten games, which tells you how the coaching staff is reading it.

He has the speed that made him a second-round pick of Ottawa in 2017, faster than 73% of the league by NHL Edge. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking has only seven games of him so far, too few to show a clear pattern. Our range says 7 to 17 goals over a full season. For a depth winger on a contender, the job is simple: win your shifts. That hasn't happened often enough yet.
headline: Formenton's depth role
